candidate.answerReason: There were 13 girls and 15 boys, receiving 169+225=394 jelly beans altogether. The class therefore had 28 students, agreeing with choice B.

methods.label: Compare nearby group sizes
methods.explanation:
Mrs. Wonderful gave away \(400-6=394\) jelly beans. Each group's bean total is its number of students multiplied by itself, because every student receives that same number of beans.

Half of \(394\) is \(197\), close to \(14\cdot14=196\), so look for group sizes near \(14\). With two more boys than girls, try \(13\) girls and \(15\) boys. Their bean totals are
\[
13\cdot13+15\cdot15=169+225=394.
\]
This is the only possible pair. Fewer than \(13\) girls would also mean fewer than \(15\) boys, making both bean totals smaller. More than \(13\) girls would make both totals larger. Thus the class had \(13+15=28\) students, choice \(\boxed{\text{B}}\).
methods.levelReason: The method uses whole-number multiplication, an estimate to locate a candidate, and comparison to exclude every other count. No quadratic-solving procedure is needed.

candidate.annotationRationale: The target is finding the integer group sizes satisfying the distribution total and the difference of two. The written route finds a candidate arithmetically and proves uniqueness by comparing larger and smaller counts. Equal-group multiplication and parts-and-total reasoning support that route.
